title: Running a band: contracts, no begging for drinks, Paul Barbarin
summary: Joseph explains his business approach: sign a contract, never ask clients for food or drink, and tells of working with Paul Barbarin and Eddie Johnson.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: But if you got contrarian fellas in the band, you never have a band. See?

You see, you got some fellas, sometimes. They get that, they all go about the money. You understand what I mean? I never make no money. When I go do my business, I do my business in the business way. I'm going to sign a contract, and I pay them off. You understand what I mean? And I don't want nobody telling me how to do and what to do and what not to do. Now, if you hire me to do something, I'm going to do like you tell me in your band.

I'm not going to, you see, nothing of a thing. You see, plenty of people don't understand this. When you're playing music, you see these people, when the people hire you, you know these people don't have to give you nothing to eat and nothing to drink.
You understand what I'm talking about?

They ain't got to give you a glass of water. You understand? Them people is paying you to play. Now, if they want to give you water, they give you water. You understand what I mean? They feel like giving you water, they give you water. Before I make the people give you nothing, them people ain't supposed to give you nothing. They ain't supposed to give you nothing. What you got, some fellas playing, they're talking, man, why don't you ask a man to give me a bottle? Okay, just a drink. You know what I tell them? I tell them all on the board and the board. I said, look, y'all going on the job. If you want to stop and get you something to drink, y'all better buy you something to drink. Now, don't ask me to ask the people for nothing to drink. And they don't ask for nothing to drink. Now, if they give us, we'll take it. But if you don't give us, I can't get mad. But you know why? I'm charging. You paying me, and I can buy what I want after. When I knock off, I buy what I want. You understand what I mean, Bill? Well, I can't just go make you give me things like that. But you got plenty of fellas, they be inspecting all that. They be inspecting you to make the people give you something, which you cannot. Now, sometimes, you play for the people, and they're hungry. And you can ask people to make the sandwich. Well, I feel embarrassed to be asking people about something. See, all I get, it's supposed to tell me, no, I can't get mad. You know what? I'm charging enough to get you on your body on your own lunch. Now, if you give me something, I'll appreciate it. If you don't give me nothing, it's all right. It's the same with me. When I knock off, I'll go out and maybe buy me something. Well, actually, I work with Paul Bobran. I've been all around the country with Paul Bobran. He can tell you the same way. Been with him. And I like Paul for this. Paul, anywhere Paul plays, you never catch Paul. Ask nobody for nothing to drink. They give Paul, it's all right. As far as him asking the people to give, no. I played at New Orleans Country Club with Paul. They didn't ask for nothing. The man said, Paul, y'all take intermission. Come on, we'll give y'all, speak something for the band. As far as asking, we didn't ask for nothing. And that's what Paul liked about me. Paul tell you the same thing. As long as I was going to go with playing with him, we never ask nobody for nothing. We never get out of our place with nobody when we were playing music. We try to satisfy the people. You understand me, Bill? Every person come and ask me, do you know this? If one of us don't know it, it's somebody in that band knows it. You see, like Eddie Johnson. Eddie Johnson knows every number. Every number you ask for, Eddie can give it to you. Well, Eddie got all kind of music in there. Paul's a good saxophone player. He's a good saxophone player. Good man. He's a good man. And what I like about Eddie, he's all, well, Eddie got some good remember, Bill. Eddie can bring some things up to you sometimes with music. You'll be surprised. That's right. He makes you play your horn. It's the number they bring up to you. And after everybody's falling,
it makes you play your horn.
